Any exit in between (File::open error, PackageReader::open error or Canceled at 2727, VerifyMismatch at 2731) leaves origin_disk holding the old fingerprint. findings.what: 'Every edit advances it by one' is false for an edit that writes the value the document already holds: chronicle returns no_change and the revision stays. The next edit then expects N+1 against N and is refused stale_revision. The caller reads the revision, gets N again, and the same command fails the same way every time.

Update the --expect-revision text in manual.rs:37 and the edit summary and harness DESCRIPTOR, which say it advances per edit, and add this command line to expect_revision_covers_every_edit_of_one_command_line.

findings.what: The temp is hashed after the compare and before the rename. That puts one full hash pass of the new package into the window the module docs admit for non-Studio writers, and into the lock hold every Studio waiter sits behind. A foreign replace during that pass is lost silently, for seconds on a large package when it could be a few syscalls.
findings.scenario: A 512 MiB package: an external tool renames its file over the destination while lines 279-280 hash the temp. The compare already passed, the rename overwrites it, nothing refuses.
findings.fix: Hash the temp first: move lines 279-280 above line 277. The rest of the function is unchanged.

findings.certainty: READ for the code; the filesystem case is not run
findings.what: DENIED_WAIT is measured from the start of acquire, not from the first denied open. A waiter that sat behind a holder for over 1 s refuses destination_read_only on its first denied open, with no retry. The module docs say a delete-pending open is retried. Reachable on a filesystem without POSIX delete, where the sidecar stays delete-pending while another waiter's handle is open (Windows delete-pending semantics on FAT, exFAT or an SMB share). NTFS on a current Windows drops the name at once, which is why the soak would not show this. The recovery text then tells the caller to make the file writable.
findings.scenario: Two waiters queued 5 s behind a save on an exFAT or SMB folder. The holder releases, waiter 1 holds its handle for a moment, waiter 2's open is denied: destination_read_only on a writable folder.
findings.fix: Track let mut denied_since: Option<Instant>; set it on the first denied open, clear it on any other outcome, and compare denied_since.elapsed() to DENIED_WAIT.min(wait).

findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-session/src/save_guard.rs:24-25 (module docs), :144-149 (stamp), :128 (Drop), and the save_safety text in crates/hsk-studio-session/src/lib.rs DESCRIPTOR
findings.what: 'Exactly one save from a revision lands' is not closed in two cases, and brief item 3 says to state a remaining race plainly. (a) Stamp collision: an orphan holder W (lock on the removed file) and the live holder C (new file at the name) compare equal when length and modified time both match. Length is 1 + (pid*31 + counter*131 + subsec_nanos) mod 65536. On NTFS (100 ns) the two clock reads must share a tick, the nanos then cancel, and pid_a*31+c_a*131 must equal pid_b*31+c_b*131 mod 65536: practically nil. On a filesystem with 1-2 s modified times (FAT, some network targets), or where set_modified fails (the ignored result at :145), time matches and the odds are 1 in 65536 per orphan race. Then W runs as a holder beside C, and W's Drop at :128 removes C's name, so a third process can also enter. (b) A filesystem whose try_lock returns Ok without sharing the lock across machines (local-only flock on an NFS nolock mount or a FUSE mount) gives two holders. Only the Unsupported case is documented.
findings.scenario: (a) Contended saves to a FAT-formatted folder. (b) Two machines saving one package on a nolock NFS mount.
findings.fix: Text only: add both cases to the 'what it does not close' paragraph and the DESCRIPTOR. The stamp itself is acceptable: std has no stable file identity on Windows.
